name: Project Crew
tagline: Group projects without the group chat meltdown
about: Project Crew sets up a team charter, splits the work fairly, turns messy meetings into minutes with owners, scripts the awkward conversation with the teammate who has gone quiet, and writes honest peer assessments.
persona: You are a calm project-team facilitator who has watched hundreds of student groups: fair, allergic to vagueness, and good at making conflict boring and procedural.

onboarding.title: Make the group work
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us about the project so plans, agendas and messages fit your team.

profile.label: Project
profile.placeholder: Marketing plan for a local café, 4,000 words + pitch

tools.title: Team charter
tools.subtitle: Roles, rules and a kickoff message

inputs.label: Members and strengths / constraints
inputs.placeholder: Ana: good writer, away 10–14 Mar; Ben: does the numbers; …

tools.prompt: Members: {members}. Grading: {grading}. Create a table (Role | Person | Responsibilities | Backup) covering coordinator, editor, research and deliverable owners, a checklist of 8 ground rules the team agrees to (response times, where files live, what happens if someone misses a deadline), a kv of the meeting rhythm (when, where, how long, who runs it), and a quote with a friendly kickoff message for the group chat that gets everyone to confirm their role.

tools.title: Split the work
tools.subtitle: Brief → tasks, owners, dates

inputs.label: Availability clashes
inputs.placeholder: Ana away 10–14 Mar, Ben has exams week 6

tools.prompt: Brief: {brief}. Availability: {avail}. Break the project into a table (Task | Owner | Est. hours | Due | Needs from others) that balances hours across the team and lands everything a week before the profile's deadline for integration. Then steps for the three integration milestones (first stitch, full draft, final polish) with what each person brings, and a callout on the highest-risk dependency and how to de-risk it now.

tools.title: Minutes from my notes
tools.subtitle: Rough notes → decisions and actions

inputs.label: Rough meeting notes
inputs.placeholder: talked about intro, Ben will do charts by fri?, need to ask tutor re word count…

tools.prompt: Notes: {notes}. Write a kv (Date, Attendees, Absent, Next meeting), bullets of decisions made (one line each, no discussion), a checklist of actions in the form 'Owner — action — due date' with any missing owner or date marked '[decide]', and a quote with a short follow-up message for the group chat so people who missed it know exactly what to do.

tools.title: The awkward conversation
tools.subtitle: Someone's not pulling their weight

inputs.label: What's happening
inputs.placeholder: Sam hasn't replied in 9 days and owns the data section

tools.prompt: Situation: {situation}. Tone: {tone}. Channel: {channel}. Explain in text the likely reasons a teammate goes quiet and why the first message should offer an exit ramp. Then a quote with the exact message to send in the chosen channel and tone, plus a second version one step firmer, steps for the escalation ladder with time limits at each rung (message → call → group meeting → tutor), and a callout on documenting contributions before escalating.

tools.title: Peer assessment
tools.subtitle: Fair, evidenced, not petty

inputs.label: What each person did
inputs.placeholder: Ana wrote sections 1–2 and edited all; Ben charts late but good; …

tools.prompt: Contributions: {contrib}. Format: {format}. Produce a table (Member | Delivered | Quality | Reliability | Suggested rating) with ratings justified by evidence not feelings, a quote with a fair written comment per member in the required format that a tutor could read without wincing, and a callout on what to do if the assessment is not anonymous.
